newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. State Senate approves budget reform bill.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. State Senate approves budget reform bill.

text.p: The New York State Senate said it approved a bill to reform the budget process, a goal that has gained increasing importance since the state this year set a new national record for tardiness.

The Senate approved the pact during Tuesday's special session, but it adjourned without approving two important tax extensions for New York City or a new bonding agency the city has proposed as a way to sidestep its debt limit.

Joseph Bruno (R-Troy), who is the Senate's majority leader, said the budget reform bill, which has yet to be acted upon by the Assembly, was supported by Gov. George Pataki. A spokesman for Assembly Speaker Sheldon Silver (D-Manhattan) was not immediately available to comment.

The Senate's bill includes the threat of putting a so-called austerity budget in place if a new agreement is not reached by the April 1 deadline. Such a pact would be the same as the previous budget but impose a 10-percent, across-the-board cut in spending. Only a few areas would be exempt from the reductions, federal funds, debt service and reappropriations.

"Having an austerity budget take effect would provide incentive for an agreement on a new budget and eliminate the need for emergency appropriation bills and uncertainity that surrounds them," Bruno said, in prepared remarks.
The bill also would impose the following new rules.
--require a governor taking office for the first time to submit a budget on the first Tuesday in January after being sworn into office.
--require the governor to submit a four-year fiscal plan at the same time as the proposed budget, and update the plan 60 days after a new budget was approved.
--simplify the budget by limiting the executive budget to a maximum of seven budget bills and no more than 10 Article 7 bills.
